checks.claim: Charge-conserving correction, dipole transformation, and smooth damped Coulomb construction
checks.explanation: No error found in the selected charge correction and damped-electrostatics derivation.
checks.demonstration: Writing qtilde=q−((1^Tq−Q)/N)1 gives1^Tqtilde=Q. The correction is the orthogonal projection onto the affine charge hyperplane: any other feasibleqtilde+z has1^Tz=0, so its squared distance fromq equals the correction norm squared plus||z||². Under r_i→Qr_i+t, the dipole transforms as p→Qp+Qtotal*t, which is the correct charged-system origin dependence. The quintic cutoffphi(x)=1−10x³+15x⁴−6x⁵ has value and first two derivatives0 atx1. Thus chi(r)=phi(2r)/sqrt(r²+1)+(1−phi(2r))/r agrees exactly with1/r forr≥R/2 and joins with two derivatives. Asr→0,1−phi(2r)=O(r³), sochi→1 andchi′→0. These identities support a smooth scalar electrostatic energy away from unrelated neural or collision singularities. Independent charge-projection, dipole and endpoint checks pass.

The dipole of a charged molecule is origin-dependent; the formula does not promise otherwise. Local message-passing invariance was inspected as context; universal accuracy and protein transferability are not mathematical consequences of these identities. The paper itself states that direct long-range pair summation is quadratic.

review-bio-icnn.version: ICML 2017 published main paper and official supplement

checks.location: Propositions 1–2, main pp. 3–4; Appendix B Eq. (22): input convexity, PICNN containment and LP epigraph inference.
checks.claim: Propositions 1–2, main pp. 3–4; Appendix B Eq. (22): input convexity, PICNN containment and LP epigraph inference.
checks.explanation: No issue was found in the checked claims. The main convexity and representation arguments hold under the stated conditions. The LP optimal-value argument is sound with that final-layer qualification; its informal assertion that all optimiser activations must be exact is stronger than needed when downstream weights vanish.
checks.demonstration: Induct on layers: nonnegative combinations of componentwise convex hidden functions remain convex; adding an affine input term preserves convexity; composing with a convex coordinatewise nondecreasing activation preserves convexity. In PICNN, fixing x makes its gating factors constants, with the hidden gates rectified to preserve nonnegativity. Setting the x pathway to zero and both gates to one recovers FICNN; placing a feedforward score in the x path and taking its final inner product with y recovers the paper’s energy representation of a feedforward network. For the ReLU LP, every exact forward activation is feasible. Conversely, reducing each slack hidden variable to its forward ReLU value can only decrease later preactivations and the nonnegative final objective, so an exact activation assignment attains an equally good or better objective. This proves optimal-value equivalence; it does not prove every LP optimiser has every hidden inequality tight when zero downstream weights make some activations irrelevant.
checks.scope: Proposition 3’s complete differentiation-through-finite-bundle-iterations claim was not independently certified; smoothness, active-set regularity and dependence of cut points require separate analysis. No general training-convergence claim is established by input convexity.
checks.claimContext: Nonnegative hidden weights and convex, nondecreasing activations preserve convexity in the designated input. The paper also gives a partial-input extension and a linear-programming formulation for inference.

review-neurips-2026-150719.title: Orthrus: Memory-Efficient Parallel Token Generation via Dual-View Diffusion

checks.location: Section3.3 diverse generation and first-divergence correction; public src/model.py498-513
checks.claim: the exact causal correction token $y_{j}$ drawn directly from $p_{\text{AR}}$
checks.explanation: If rejection is followed by an independent fresh draw from \(p\), the resulting output law is generally not \(p\). The standard residual correction restores the exact law. The author-linked implementation at the linked commit uses that residual branch, so the description needs to distinguish residual correction after rejection from direct-target sampling for the bonus token. A target-first coupling can also make direct-target wording valid; the acceptance/coupling rule must be specified.
checks.demonstration:
Under standard acceptance at a fixed accepted prefix, retained mass is \(m(v)=\min(p(v),q(v))\) and rejection probability is \(R=1-\sum_v m(v)\). An independent fresh target draw after rejection gives
\[
\Pr(Y=v)=m(v)+R\,p(v),
\]
which need not equal \(p(v)\).

Take \(p=(4/5,1/5)\) and \(q=(1/5,4/5)\). Standard acceptance contributes \((1/5,1/5)\) and rejects with probability \(R=3/5\). Fresh-target correction then yields
\[
\left(\frac15,\frac15\right)+\frac35\left(\frac45,\frac15\right)
=\left(\frac{17}{25},\frac8{25}\right)\ne p.
\]
The residual law instead gives \(\min(p,q)+[p-q]_+=p\) coordinatewise. Greedy replacement by the AR argmax is likewise exact by induction on the accepted prefix. If an independent target token is sampled first and the proposal is retained exactly when it equals that same token, the output is always the pre-sampled target; that alternative coupling is a valid positive case.

At commit 4dceab65156b3dfb5dadbb11181a0e65d0ad314d, lines 498–513 implement ratio acceptance and the normalized positive residual. Direct-target sampling after all proposals are accepted supplies the bonus token and is correct for that different event. This source supports the ideal residual construction rather than the literal fresh-target-on-rejection interpretation. This comparison does not certify every numerical tolerance or floating-point execution path.
checks.repair:
For standard speculative acceptance, specify the rejected-token law explicitly:
\[
r(v)=\frac{[p(v)-q(v)]_+}{R}\qquad(R>0).
\]
Then accepted mass plus correction mass equals \(p\). At successive prefixes, \(q\) must be the actual proposal conditional law for that prefix; this is needed for a complete block-level argument. Keep direct \(p\) for an unconstrained bonus token or describe the alternative target-first coupling precisely. The linked author code already supplies the ideal residual correction. The mathematical proof concerns the specified probability law under ideal arithmetic; it is separate from a guarantee for every finite-precision execution.
checks.scope: The stochastic correction prescription under standard speculative acceptance, with the current code’s valid ideal residual branch distinguished. Greedy parity and the ideal residual algorithm remain valid.
checks.title: Rejected proposals require a residual correction under standard speculative acceptance
checks.claimFormula: Y_{\rm corr}\sim p_{\rm AR}\quad\text{on rejection},\qquad\mathcal L(Y_{\rm out})=p_{\rm AR}\quad\text{(claimed)}
checks.whyItMatters: The stochastic guarantee needs the correct correction law or an explicit coupling, rather than an unqualified direct-target draw.
checks.claimContext: Section 3.3 introduces diverse generation with exact rejection sampling, then says that at the first divergence the causal correction token is drawn directly from \(p_{\rm AR}\). At a fixed accepted prefix, let \(p\) be the target token law and \(q\) the proposal law. Under standard speculative acceptance, a proposal \(X\sim q\) is retained with probability \(\min(1,p(X)/q(X))\).

Proof Step 6 reverses this direction when deriving a lower bound on $\mathbb E\|e_t^{\mathrm{open}}\|^2$. The contracting drift $F(s)=-s$ obeys the upper condition and makes the prediction error shrink.
checks.demonstration:
Take the scalar drift $F(s)=-s$, giving dynamics $\dot s=-s$, with true state $s_0=0$, initial prediction $\widehat s_0=1$, and unit time steps. The drift is $1$-Lipschitz and the exact flow is $\Phi_1(s)=e^{-1}s$, which satisfies Assumption A5. Set process noise, measurement noise and bias to zero. For the associated closed-loop system choose $K=3/4$ and $W=0$. These satisfy A6–A9 and give $\alpha=(1+1)(1-3/4)=1/2<1$. The theorem expressly defines its open-loop comparison by setting $K=0$; the positive gain restriction applies to the associated closed-loop system.

The open-loop error is therefore
$$e_t^{\mathrm{open}}=e^{-t},\qquad \mathbb E|e_t^{\mathrm{open}}|^2=e^{-2t}.$$
Equation (13) instead requires this quantity to be at least $4^t$. At the first step,
$$e^{-2}\approx0.1353<4.$$
This satisfies the stated hypotheses and directly contradicts the claimed lower bound. A positive noise variance does not repair the implication: independent centered process noise of variance $0.01$ gives one-step mean-squared error $e^{-2}+0.01\approx0.1453<4$.
checks.repair:
Use the upper estimate supplied by A5. Put $a=1+L_F\Delta t$ and write the open-loop error as
$$e_{t+1}=\Phi(\widehat s_t)-\Phi(s_t)-w_{t+1}.$$
Assume $\|\Phi(x)-\Phi(y)\|\leq a\|x-y\|$, with the current states measurable from the past $\mathcal F_t$, and innovations satisfying
$$\mathbb E[w_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]=0,\qquad
\mathbb E[\|w_{t+1}\|^2\mid\mathcal F_t]\leq v.$$
The conditional cross term vanishes, so
$$\mathbb E\|e_{t+1}\|^2\leq a^2\mathbb E\|e_t\|^2+v.$$
Iterating gives the valid bound
$$\mathbb E\|e_t\|^2\leq a^{2t}\mathbb E\|e_0\|^2+v\sum_{j=0}^{t-1}a^{2j}.$$
It bounds possible amplification. For a lower growth bound, add the separate expansion hypothesis $\|\Phi(x)-\Phi(y)\|\geq m\|x-y\|$ with $m>1$ and the same conditional centering. The nonnegative innovation variance then gives $\mathbb E\|e_{t+1}\|^2\geq m^2\mathbb E\|e_t\|^2$, hence $\mathbb E\|e_t\|^2\geq m^{2t}\mathbb E\|e_0\|^2$. This additional hypothesis excludes contracting dynamics and is not implied by A5.
checks.scope: The affected statements are the universal open-loop lower bound in Theorem A.3, equation (13), and its recurrence in equation (25), in the public extended manuscript. The contraction witness does not refute the distinct closed-loop upper estimate.
checks.whyItMatters: The claimed comparison requires every admitted open-loop predictor to amplify error. The admissible contraction instead gives $\mathbb E|e_t^{\mathrm{open}}|^2=e^{-2t}$, so the theorem cannot establish that universal instability or the resulting contrast with closed-loop stability.

checks.location: Lemma A.1(ii), Eq. (11) and closing convergence assertion; work/text/153606.txt:1666
checks.claim:
The residual error of the Newton step is
 $\mathbf{S}_{t}^{+}-\mathbf{S}^{\star}_{t}=O\!\big(\lVert\mathbf{S}_{t}^{-}-\mathbf{S}^{\star}_{t}\rVert^{2}\big)$ .
checks.explanation: The proof correctly names the Hessian condition required by the standard local Newton theorem. The statement permits a smooth residual whose curvature cancels the positive Gaussian terms, leaving a degenerate minimum. At such a minimum, a Newton step can reduce error only linearly. The missing hypothesis concerns the full objective Hessian, not positivity of the two covariance arrays.
checks.demonstration:
Use the scalar setting with $P^-=R_{\mathrm{obs}}=1$, prior mean $S^-=h$, virtual observation $Z_{\mathrm{obs}}=-h$, and
$$\Psi(s)=s^4-s^2.$$
The residual is $C^\infty$, and equation (10) becomes
$$\mathcal F_h(s)=\frac12(s-h)^2+\frac12(-h-s)^2+\Psi(s)=s^4+h^2.$$
Its unique minimizer is $S^\star=0$. For every $h\neq0$, the Hessian at the starting point is positive and invertible, so the displayed Newton step exists:
$$S^+=h-\frac{\mathcal F_h'(h)}{\mathcal F_h''(h)}
=h-\frac{4h^3}{12h^2}=\frac23h.$$
Consequently,
$$\frac{|S^+-S^\star|}{|S^--S^\star|^2}=\frac{2}{3|h|}\longrightarrow\infty.$$
The objectives differ only by an additive constant, so their gradients, Hessians, minimizer, and Newton map are identical. This is a fixed Newton map near a degenerate minimum, not a change in curvature hidden in the limiting argument. At the minimizer, $\mathcal F_h''(0)=0$. The example therefore satisfies the printed lemma but fails the positive-definite-Hessian condition explicitly named at the end of its proof.
checks.repair:
Add the condition already invoked in the proof: $\nabla^2\mathcal F(S^\star)\succ0$, and require the initial point to be sufficiently close to $S^\star$. Together with the stated $C^3$ regularity, this yields a ball around $S^\star$ and constants $\mu>0$, $L_H<\infty$ such that
$$H(x):=\nabla^2\mathcal F(x)\succeq\mu I,\qquad
\|H(x)-H(y)\|\leq L_H\|x-y\|.$$
For $e=x-S^\star$, the Newton error satisfies
$$x^+-S^\star
=H(x)^{-1}\int_0^1\bigl[H(x)-H(S^\star+te)\bigr]e\,dt,$$
using $\nabla\mathcal F(S^\star)=0$. Hence
$$\|x^+-S^\star\|\leq\frac{L_H}{2\mu}\|x-S^\star\|^2.$$
Choose the starting error inside the ball and small enough that $L_H\|e\|/(2\mu)\leq1/2$. Subsequent errors stay in that ball, so the same bound proves local quadratic convergence. This makes the proof's existing condition explicit in the lemma.
checks.scope: The correction is to the hypotheses of the quadratic Newton-error assertion in Lemma A.1(ii). The original proof already invokes positive definiteness for its cited result. The purely Gaussian case in part (i) has a positive-definite full Hessian and is unaffected.
checks.whyItMatters: The claimed quadratic rate does not apply to every smooth residual allowed by the lemma. Stating the Hessian and local-initialization conditions specifies when the rate is valid.
checks.title: The Newton-rate statement omits the Hessian condition used in its proof
checks.claimContext: Lemma A.1 starts from the variational objective in equation (10), positive diagonal covariances $P^-$ and $R_{\mathrm{obs}}$, a residual potential $\Psi\in C^3$, and a local minimizer $S^\star$. Part (ii) claims a quadratic error after one Newton step from the prior mean $S^-$. The proof subsequently invokes positive definiteness of the full Hessian, but the lemma and its standing assumptions do not impose it.

aerochem-open-loop-error-bound.issueTitle: A contracting system contradicts the error lower bound
aerochem-open-loop-error-bound.plainExplanation: An upper Lipschitz condition permits the contracting dynamics $F(s)=-s$, so it cannot imply the claimed open-loop error growth. Separately, the Newton-rate lemma omits the positive-definite-Hessian condition that its own proof invokes.
aerochem-open-loop-error-bound.paperSummary: AeroChem couples a physical process branch with learned virtual measurements and state correction to forecast chemically reactive air quality over long horizons.
aerochem-open-loop-error-bound.theoryRole: The appendix's open-loop lower bound is intended to contrast open-loop drift with closed-loop stability. This comparison is stronger than saying that some open-loop systems can amplify errors.
